sources.title: საქართველოს მთავრობის დადგენილება №447 — წყლის რესურსების მონიტორინგის დაგეგმვისა და განხორციელების წესის დამტკიცების შესახებ
საქართველოს კანონი „წყლის რესურსების მართვის შესახებ“ — კონსოლიდირებული ვერსია

requirements.requirement: NEA prepares the State Water Resources Monitoring Plan annually and submits it to the Minister for approval no later than 1 December each year.
requirements.note: The decree does not state in this article which plan-year label must be used. Do not claim that the next plan has or has not been submitted before the deadline.

requirements.requirement: Monitoring data are stored in standardized formats for national reports and river-basin management plans; access is provided subject to environmental-information access, data-protection and confidentiality law.
The state monitoring plan is representative and risk-based, uses standardized methods/indices for temporal comparability, documents background values and justifies representative monitoring/grouping.
The state system includes hydrological, hydrochemical, hydrobiological, hydromorphological and hydrogeological programmes for surface-water and groundwater bodies.

The need, sites, microbiological parameters, frequency and methods are determined by water-body type, existing or likely pressures, water use, microbiological contamination risk and monitoring objectives.
Operational monitoring applies to water bodies at risk, covers significant pressures and evaluates measure effectiveness; the rule describes high frequency as monthly or quarterly.
Investigative monitoring is triggered by pollution incidents/accidents or when the reason for failure to achieve good status is unknown; it is flexible and problem-oriented.

Priority-substance monitoring in biota and sediment is introduced progressively. Until full implementation, chemical-status assessment may mainly rely on water-column results. For substances requiring biota/sediment assessment, monitoring must start no later than 2028-01-01.
requirements.note: This deadline applies to substances whose assessment requires these matrices, not indiscriminately to every analyte.

requirements.requirement: By 2027-09-01, the Minister must ensure identification of nitrate-contaminated or nitrate-risk zones in surface water and groundwater, identify nitrate-vulnerable zones, and define good agricultural practice rules and action plans for those zones.
requirements.responsible: Minister, as named in the Law
requirements.note: This is a future statutory milestone as of 2026-11-28; it is not evidence that the zones or action plans have already been completed.

scope_boundaries.fact: Decree 447 regulates the state water-resource monitoring system for surface-water and groundwater bodies. The consolidated Water Resources Management Law separately assigns the National Food Agency state control of drinking-water quality (Article 31(3)).
scope_boundaries.implication: Do not apply Decree 447's water-body monitoring frequency or matrix rules as if they were consumer tap-water compliance thresholds.

scope_boundaries.fact: The consolidated Water Resources Management Law Article 37(1)(b)(b) sets 2027-09-01 as the deadline for adopting the technical regulation on water quality intended for human consumption; Article 42(3) sets the relevant provisions' commencement date at 2027-09-01.
scope_boundaries.implication: This is a future statutory milestone as of 2026-11-28, not proof that the technical regulation is already adopted or in force.

scope_boundaries.fact: The Water Resources Management Law Article 37(2)(b)(c)-(e) sets a 2027-09-01 deadline for identifying nitrate-contaminated or at-risk surface-water and groundwater zones, nitrate-vulnerable zones, and related good-agricultural-practice rules/action plans.
scope_boundaries.implication: AquaSignal must track the legal milestone separately from observed nitrate concentrations and from consumer drinking-water compliance; the law does not provide the completed zone map or monitoring results.

aqua_signal_design_implications: Store water matrix and point-of-use context explicitly: surface water, groundwater, coastal/transitional water, raw source water, treatment-plant outlet and distribution/tap water are not interchangeable.
Represent monitoring programme and trigger separately: observational, operational and investigative; keep monthly/quarterly operational frequency distinct from risk-based observational schedules.
Record the reason for microbiological monitoring (water-body type, pressure, use, contamination risk, objective) and the sampling method, QA/QC and denominator.

For priority substances, store water-column, biota and sediment results as separate matrices with their own units, detection limits and dates; apply the 2028 transition only to substances requiring those matrices.
Track the annual monitoring-plan submission as a dated milestone; on 2026-12-01 verify publication/submission status rather than presuming it.

Track nitrate-vulnerable-zone identification, good agricultural practice rules and action plans as a separate 2027-09-01 statutory milestone; do not infer completion from nitrate concentration records.
not_established: The 2026-12-01 annual submission has not yet been verified; it is an upcoming deadline on the review date.
The decree does not provide the actual monitoring-station inventory, 2027 schedule, sample counts, analytical results, laboratory detection limits or current compliance rates.
The annex DOCX was not independently downloaded in this run; the structured requirements above are drawn from the official Matsne HTML body, not unverified annex tables.
The decree does not itself establish consumer tap-water concentration limits or replace the separate drinking-water technical regulation.
The nitrate-vulnerable zones, good agricultural practice rules and action plans due by 2027-09-01 have not been verified as completed in this review.
